newsitem.title: UK: Coffee seen heading for deficit in 1997/98 - GNI.
newsitem.headline: Coffee seen heading for deficit in 1997/98 - GNI.

text.p: The world coffee market could be faced with a substantial supply deficit in 1997/98 (Oct-Sept) if consumption growth remains strong and forecasts of a lower Brazilian crop proved correct, broker GNI said.

In the November issue of its Commodity Perspective report, GNI said there was a growing consensus that Brazil's 1997/98 crop, now at the flowering stage, would be lower than 1996/97's harvest of around 25-26 million 60-kg bags.

"While estimates will not be available until mid-November at the earliest (and end-January for an accurate one), some agronomists are already talking about a crop in the region of 20 to 22 million bags," GNI said.
"If these figures prove to be correct, and consumption continues at the rate of growth seen over the past few years, the world could be faced with a substantial deficit next year," it added.
"GNI is currently compiling its outlook for next year and will be making significant changes to its old 1996/97 estimate (unchanged for nearly a year now)."

"But it is fair to say that if supply and demand are taken to be in balance in the 1996/97 coffee year, then a deficit in the order of six million bags could be seen in 1997/98 (if the Brazilian forecast is proved correct)," it added.

GNI said while the combined stocks of the Brazilian government and the Colombian Coffee Federation were ample to offset the projected imbalance, they were unlikely to release sufficient stocks unless prices dictate such action.
"Bears beware," said GNI. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
